research:
I'm writing up the findings now, using only information dated on or before 2026-09-22. The AAA site and several article pages refused the connection, so the AAA figures below come from search snippets and press coverage.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the AAA "current avg" for regular gas on gasprices.aaa.com on 2026-10-01. I couldn't load the page directly because the proxy refused it. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/)
- 2026-09-22: Coverage citing AAA put the national average for regular at **$4.47**. The headline says the average "remains well over $4.40." [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/gas-prices-09-22-26-142109535.html)
- 2026-09-17: AAA's weekly report put the average at $4.43, up 16 cents from a week earlier. A snippet of AAA's daily data gives one exact figure of $4.4386. [AAA newsroom](https://newsroom.aaa.com/2026/09/national-average-climbs-nearly-5-cents-since-last-week/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. On 2026-09-22 the average was about $4.47, roughly 7 cents above the $4.40 threshold, with 9 days to go. A drop of more than about 7 cents by October 1 would resolve it No; holding flat or rising would resolve it Yes.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-22: Brent was about $99.9 a barrel and WTI about $95.3. Iran signaled it could reopen transit through the Strait of Hormuz within a week if the US eased military pressure and lifted its blockade on Iranian ports. No deal had been announced. [Mezha](https://mezha.net/eng/?p=3726310)
- About 2026-09-20: ABC reported the average was nearing $4.48 and diesel hit a record $6.49. It also said 2026 set a record for the most days above $4 in a calendar year. [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/Business/gas-prices-set-record-highest-number-days-4/story?id=137253203)
- 2026-09-17: AAA's report "Pump Prices Keep Climbing as Crude Oil Remains High" said crude was averaging about $100 a barrel and prices were more than $1 above a year earlier. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/2026/09/)
- 2026-09-10: AAA put the average at $4.27, up 13 cents in a week as crude climbed. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/2026/09/)
- 2026-09-03: AAA put the average at $4.14, up 4 cents in a week. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/2026/09/)
- Industry groups say both global supply shocks (Hormuz, Venezuela) and limited US refinery capacity are pushing pump prices up. [CNY Central](https://cnycentral.com/news/nation-world/gallery/oil-group-says-global-supply-shocks-us-refinery-limits-are-both-driving-pump-pain-gulf-coast-venezuela-strait-hormuz?photo=1)

## 4. Base rates
- **Trend:** about $4.10 in late August, $4.14 on Sept 3, $4.27 on Sept 10, $4.43 on Sept 17 and about $4.47 on Sept 22. That is roughly a 37-cent rise in a month, but the rise slowed to about +4 cents between Sept 17 and Sept 22.
- **2026 high so far:** $4.564 on May 21. [Action Network](https://www.actionnetwork.com/prediction-markets/how-high-will-gas-prices-get-kalshi-odds)
- **Typical size of moves:** In calm periods the AAA average usually moves less than 5 cents over 9 days. In shock periods like 2022 and September 2026 it can move 10 to 20 cents a week. Retail prices typically react to a change in crude within about 1 to 2 weeks and fall more slowly than they rise ("rockets and feathers"). That is general knowledge, not something I found in a source.
- **Seasonal pattern:** After the switch to cheaper winter-blend gasoline (allowed from Sept 15), prices usually drift lower from late September into October, unless crude or refinery shocks override it.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi runs weekly and monthly AAA gas-price markets (series KXAAAGASW and KXAAAGASM). I couldn't find prices for October 1 thresholds dated on or before the cutoff. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/category/economics/oil-and-energy)
- Manifold has related markets, for example "US average gas price is $4.100 or more." I didn't retrieve their probabilities. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Jack1/us-average-gas-price-is-4100-or-mor)
- Spring 2026: Treasury Secretary Bessent was optimistic gas could return to about $3 between June 20 and September 20. That clearly did not happen. [WJLA](https://wjla.com/news/nation-world/scott-bessent-says-gas-could-be-3-between-june-and-september-treasury-donald-trump-oil-strait-of-hormuz-iran)

## 6. Upcoming events before October 1
- **Iran and Hormuz:** a possible reopening within about a week, or a US-Iran deal, could push crude down sharply. Any new escalation, such as more strikes, would push prices up. Because pump prices lag crude, only a crude move in the next few days would show up fully by October 1.
- **EIA weekly petroleum status reports:** about Sept 23 and Sept 30, covering gasoline inventories and refinery utilization.
- **AAA weekly update:** about Sept 24.
- **Hurricane season:** still active, so a storm hitting Gulf Coast refineries remains a risk.
- **Winter-blend transition:** continuing seasonal downward pressure.

  - The winter-blend transition after Sept 15 adds seasonal downward pressure.
  - On 2026-09-22, Iran signaled it could reopen Hormuz within a week if the US eased its blockade. A deal could cut crude sharply.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: A US-Iran understanding is announced around Sept 24-26. Brent falls to the mid-$80s and wholesale gasoline drops about 30 cents. Combined with cheaper winter blend, retail falls 1 to 2 cents a day, and AAA shows about $4.37 on Oct 1.
- Yes: No deal materializes or talks stall. Crude stays around $95 to $100 and retail drifts sideways or slightly down to about $4.42 to $4.50 by Oct 1.

(f) Adjustment: I start at about 75%. I move down slightly for three reasons:
- The price appears to have peaked around Sept 20.
- The seasonal blend switch pushes prices lower.
- The Hormuz news is a credible near-term path to a large crude drop.

The lag in retail pass-through limits how much of any crude drop shows up by Oct 1, so I don't move far. I land at about 70%.

Probability: 70%
